description.narrative:
The Development and Partnership in Action (DPA) program operates in three districts, two of which—O’Reang and Keo Seima—have been selected for the Strengthening Civic Engagement and Oversight in Public Financial Management (SCOPE PFM) initiative.
DPA conducted nine Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with 75 participants comprising Communal Land Titling (CLT) committee members, Indigenous youth, four commune councilors, village chiefs, teachers, school principals, and general citizens across three CLTs. The findings revealed significant gaps in public finance knowledge, engagement, and participation. Respondents indicated that no community groups currently work on public finance issues—such as searching for budget information and legal frameworks, raising community awareness, collecting inputs for consultations on new or amended policies, mobilizing community participation in Commune Development Plans (CDPs) and Commune Investment Plans (CIPs), or monitoring local budget allocations and expenditures.
Regarding awareness of their rights and opportunities within commune-level Public Financial Management (PFM), all respondents were unaware of their right to participate in Commune and District Council meetings. Most did not know that Commune Councils (CCs) have funds to support public services, education,natural resource management (NRM), and other community services, although some were aware of basic registration services and children’s education. In terms of engagement with Commune Councils and public finance processes, all respondents reported never having been invited by CCs to participate in CDP and CIP planning processes. Community needs have never been raised or discussed in CC meetings. Most respondents also stated that they lack sufficient knowledge and confidence—particularly regarding financial management, budgeting, and expenditure—which prevents effective participation in CC meetings.
Respondents have not accessed budget related information from any source, either online or offline. They have also not participated in awareness raising events, training, or other PFM related activities organized by CCs or other organizations. To build confidence and strengthen the capacity of CLT committees and Community Youth Groups (CYGs), as well as student parent committee members, it is essential to enhance their skills and knowledge in public financial management for local decision making and advocacy. Key areas include: community group formation and functioning; meeting facilitation and awareness raising skills; communication and engagement with local authorities at district, provincial, and national levels; digital literacy for accessing and sharing information; understanding CDP, CIP, and local budgeting processes; and mobilizing group members to participate in PFM related events. For the general population, it is critical to increase awareness of the roles and responsibilities of Commune Councils, citizens’ rights to participate in CC meetings, and opportunities to provide input onPFM issues related to public services, education, natural resource management, and other sectors, thereby contributing to greater budget transparency and accountability at the commune level.

participating-org.narrative: Development and Partnership in Action (DPA) is a non-political, non-religious, non- partisan, non-profit making Cambodian non-governmental organization devoted to furthering community development, partnership work with Cambodian NGOs and lobbying and advocacy. DPA is the successor of CIDSE Cambodia which was established in 1979 as part of the larger CIDSE CLV programme created by a consortiumof International NGOs from Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. With a mission spanning more than 25 years,the milestones andachievements of CIDSE Cambodia are significant, not least of which is moving from meeting basic daily needs of beneficiaries to focusing on strategic long-term aims of building capacity and empowering partner organizations to assist in changing their target communities lives. CIDSE Cambodia began funding CNGOS in 1993 and formally established the Partnership Programme in 1994. Due to the evolving social climate and the strong capacity and commitment of its local staff, CIDSE Cambodia decided to localize and in 1996 began a transition process which enabled the organization to emerge as DPA in January 2006. DPA assumed responsibility for all work of CIDSE Cambodia from 1 January 2006, with an emphasis on community organizing (CO) and rights-based (RB) strategies.
